title: They Banned My $35K/Month Page So I Started a Business
channel: Chris Koerner on The Koerner Office Podcast
promo_conflict: Host sells the Plans of Granger product he launches in the video and points viewers to a discount link in the description (L0630). He also repeatedly praises Beehiiv ('I love Beehive', 'the best newsletter platform in the world') and recommends Namecheap, though he says the Namecheap mention is not an ad. Revenue figures come from his own Stripe screenshots, but some of them conflict or are garbled (e.g. '$2,21', '$10,22', '5% more money per person'). The final '$30-40k net profit' includes forecasts generated by Claude.

stated_problem.quote: I need to replace that missing income.
stated_problem.speaker: Chris Koerner

idea.name: Plans of Granger creator-growth library
idea.one_liner: A one-time-payment ($47/$97, later $291) library of existing creator-growth training videos, guides and tracking spreadsheets, plus 12 recorded AMAs, sold by email to his own newsletter list and hosted on Google Drive and then a Skool community.
idea.customer: Newsletter subscribers who want to go viral, build a following or a brand (faceless or otherwise)
idea.offer: Lifetime access to unpublished training videos, docs, guides and tracking spreadsheets from his past $10k/month consulting, ongoing additions, 12 AMAs, all in a Skool community
idea.revenue_model: One-time lifetime payment through Stripe payment links ($47 vs $97 A/B tested; settled on $97; 'full price' $291 promised after launch)

key_quotes.quote: I have a treasure trove of videos, spreadsheets, and docs in my Google Drive account that has never been published.
And almost all of that is profit because we're selling a Google Drive folder at the end of the day.
So the lesson, tell them the price in the email.
That's the awesome thing about having a newsletter is there's trust.
Also, there's a lot more friction on the school landing page to pay.

acquisition_channels.details: Emails to his own Beehiiv newsletter list (~10k segment in the first test, about a quarter of the list across the A/B tests, then the rest of the list). He A/B tested price, email length, showing vs hiding the price, and Stripe vs Skool links.
YouTube video documenting the launch, with a discount link in the description.

ideas.delivery: Existing content in a Google Drive folder, shown after Stripe payment by redirect. A business partner (Kamal) later moved it into a Skool community and buyers are invited automatically. The founder records new content and runs 12 recorded AMAs.
ideas.other_uk_rules: PECR/UK GDPR: marketing emails to your own list need consent or a valid soft opt-in. Consumer Contracts Regs: digital content sold to consumers needs 14-day cancellation rights or an explicit waiver before access. DMCC Act 2024 unfair-practice rules: a 'pre-sale discount' against a $291 reference price must be genuine. Charity-linked promotion claims must be accurate.

stated_problem.quote: So immediately six figures of income to me to my family disappears overnight.
stated_problem.speaker: Chris Koerner

idea.name: Facebook content page monetization
idea.one_liner: A large Facebook page (1.5M followers) run with a content team that earned about $35k/month until Meta removed it for alleged IP infringement.
idea.customer: Facebook audience / Meta's creator monetization (monetization mechanics not detailed here)
idea.offer: Content posted to a Facebook page
idea.revenue_model: Facebook creator monetization (details not stated in this transcript); follower data also used to make ads profitable

key_quotes.quote: Most of you saw it about making 35 grand a month on Facebook.
So, not only do six figures of income disappear overnight, but I can't run ads nearly as effectively anymore

claims.claim: About $35k/month from Facebook
claims.quote: Most of you saw it about making 35 grand a month on Facebook.

claims.claim: Hundreds of thousands of dollars a year lost
claims.quote: Hundreds of thousands of dollars a year.

claims.claim: Not 100% profit; content team costs
claims.quote: This is not like a 100% profit business.

claims.claim: 1.5 million Facebook followers
claims.quote: because I needed those 1.5 million Facebook followers as data points so my ads could be profitable.

acquisition_channels.details: Ran ads that relied on page follower data.

ideas.delivery: A paid content team produces posts for the Facebook page. It carries platform risk: the page was removed with no successful appeal.
ideas.other_uk_rules: Copyright/IP compliance on reposted content; ASA/CAP rules if monetized through sponsored posts.

idea.name: Small-list weekly newsletter (Beehiiv founder)

key_quotes.quote: There's a lot of power in small email lists because you can connect so much more closely with your audience.

claims.claim: Beehiiv founder makes $500k/year from a smaller list with one email a week
claims.quote: but he makes $500,000 a year from a list much smaller than mine, and he only sends one email per week.

claims.claim: 2,000 subscribers could make tens of thousands a year
claims.quote: Even if you only had 2,000 email subscribers, you can make tens of thousands of dollars plus a year.

idea.one_liner: Selling high-ticket courses and events to a small, engaged email list.

key_quotes.quote: Events and high ticket courses are the key.
So, if you're confident in the value you're offering, then own it.
